questions.question: A class of organic compounds that contain an oxygen between two alkyl groups is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ether.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ether:-**

 
 
• It is a class of **organic compounds** that contains an **oxygen atom** between** two alkyl groups.**
 
• The general formula for an ether is **R-O-R'**, where .**R and R' are alkyl groups**
 
• Ethers are commonly used as **solvents** in various industries, including** pharmaceuticals, paints, and coatings.**
 
• Ethers are less reactive than** alcohols, aldehydes, and ketones** because the **C-O bond** is relatively **stable.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alcohol:-**

 
 
• **​** A class of organic compounds that contains a** hydroxyl (-OH) group** attached to a carbon atom.
 
• They are commonly used a**s solvents, disinfectants, and fuels.**
 
 
 
• **Aldehyde:-**
 
 
• **​** A class of organic compounds that contains a **carbonyl group (-CHO)** attached to a **carbon atom** at the end of the molecule. 
 
• They are commonly used in the production of **plastics, resins, and dyes.**
 
 
 
• **Ketone:-**
 
 
• A class of organic compounds that contains a** carbonyl group (-C=O) **attached to a carbon atom in the middle of the molecule.
 
• They are commonly used in the production of **solvents, polymers, and pharmaceuticals.**

questions.question: The Cabinet Mission came to India in ___________ to discuss the ultimate transfer of power.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1946.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cabinet Mission:-**

 
 
• It​ was a **high-level delegation** sent by the **British government to India** in **1946.**
 
• The mission was sent to discuss the** transfer of power** from **British rule to Indian hands.**
 
• The Cabinet Mission proposed a plan for a** united India** with a** federal government, **but with autonomy for **Muslim-majority provinces.**
 
• The mission's proposals were** rejected **by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League, leading to the **partition of India **and the creation of **Pakistan.**
 
• The Cabinet Mission was headed by Sir Stafford Cripps, who had previously been involved in negotiations with Indian leaders during World War II. 
 
• The mission's proposals were known as the Cripps Plan and were seen as a last-ditch effort to keep India united under British rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In ****1945**, the Second World War was still ongoing and the British government had not yet decided on the future of India.
 
• **In 1943**, the British government was still focused on the war effort and had not yet considered transferring power to India.
 
• **1942** was the year of the Quit India movement and the British government was not considering any transfer of power at that time.

questions.question: Where does the Bay of Bengal Monsoon Branch and Arabian Sea Branch merge?

options.text: North Western Part of Ganga Plains

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North Western Part of Ganga Plains.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bay of Bengal Monsoon Branch** and **Arabian Sea Branch:-**

 
 
• These merge in the **North Western Part of Ganga Plains**, which is also known as the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** or the **Northern Plains.**
 
• This region is located in the northern part of India and is formed by the alluvial deposits of the** Ganges, Brahmaputra, and their tributaries.**
 
• The merging of the** two monsoon branches** leads to** heavy rainfall in this region**, which is crucial for** agriculture** and the overall economy of the country.
 
• The **Arabian Sea Branch **of the monsoon brings rainfall to the **western coast of India**, while the **Bay of Bengal **Branch brings rainfall to the **eastern coast.**
 
• The merging of these two branches results in** widespread rainfall** in the North Western Part of Ganga Plains.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Southern Part of Peninsular:-**

 
 
• This region is **not** the location where the Bay of Bengal Monsoon Branch and Arabian Sea Branch merge.
 
• The southern part of the peninsular region receives rainfall from the **South West Monsoon,** which is a separate monsoon system.
 
 
 
• Coromandel Coast:-
 
 
• The Coromandel Coast is located in the **eastern part of India** and receives rainfall from the Bay of Bengal Monsoon Branch.
 
• However, this region is** not** the location where the two monsoon branches merge.
 
 
 
• North of Deccan Plateau:-
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau region located in **central and southern India.** 
 
• The North of the Deccan Plateau is **not **the location where the two monsoon branches merge.

questions.question: Which element's atomic number in the periodic table is named seaborgium, according to the notation of IUPAC nomenclature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**106.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seaborgium:-**

 
 
• It is a **synthetic chemical element **with the symbol **Sg** and atomic number **106.**
 
• The element was named after **Glenn T. Seaborg,** who was an** American nuclear chemist** and** Nobel laureate.**
 
• Seaborgium is a **highly radioactive element, **and its most stable isotope has a** half-life** of only a few minutes.
 
• The discovery of seaborgium was first reported in** 1974 **by a team of scientists at the **Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in California.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table:-**

 
 
• **It is a tabular arrangement of chemical elements, organized based on their atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties.**
 
• The vertical columns in the periodic table are called groups or families. Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties due to having the same number of valence electrons.
 
• 
 
The horizontal rows in the periodic table are called periods. There are seven periods, and elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.

questions.question: Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, how many inland waterways have been declared as 'national waterways'?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **The National Waterways Act, 2016:-**

 
 
• It was enacted to provide for the** development, maintenance, and regulation **of **inland waterways** for **navigation and shipping.**
 
• The Act also provides for the declaration of certain inland waterways as** 'national waterways'** by the** central government, **based on their potential for development and** transportation of goods and passengers.**
 
• The development of **national waterways** is expected to boost **inland water transport, reduce transportation costs,** and promote** economic growth and regional connectivity.**
 
• **111 inland waterways have been declared as 'national waterways' under the National Waterways Act, 2016.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inland waterways:-**

 
 
• These​ are water bodies such as** rivers, canals, lakes, and lagoons** that are used for t**ransportation, recreation, irrigation,** and other purposes.
 
• The development of inland waterways has been a priority for the **Indian government** to reduce congestion on** roads and railways, promote sustainable transportation**, and enhance **trade and tourism.**
 
• Some of the major national waterways in India include the **Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system**, the** Brahmaputra river**, the **West Coast Canal in Kerala**, and the **Godavari-Krishna river system** in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
 
• The development of national waterways involves various activities such as **dredging, construction of terminals, jetties, and navigational aids**, and provision of facilities for cargo and passenger handling.

questions.question: Creaming fat and sugar, whipping egg whites, or whipping heavy cream are examples of what type of leavening?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mechanical leavening.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mechanical leavening:-**

 
 
• It refers to the **physical process **of incorporating air into a mixture to create** lift and volume.**
 
• Creaming fat and sugar, whipping egg whites, or whipping heavy cream are examples of mechanical leavening.
 
• This is different from chemical leavening, which involves a chemical reaction to produce gas and create a rise
 
• **Creaming fat and sugar** involves beating the two together until they are **light and fluffy**.
 
• This creates air pockets in the mixture, which will **expand when heated** and create a leavening effect in baked goods.
 
• **Whipping egg whites** and **heavy cream** are similar processes that also incorporate air into the mixture.
 
• In the case of egg whites, the** proteins in the egg** form a network that traps air bubbles.
 
• Heavy cream contains **fat globules** that can also trap air.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Organic leavening:-**

 
 
• It refers to the use of **natural fermentation** to create lift in **dough or batter**.
 
• This can be achieved through the use of** sourdough starter**, for example.
 
 
 
• **Physical leavening:-**
 
 
• It​ refers to the use of **steam **or other physical processes to create lift.
 
• This can be seen in the use of steam in **bread baking**, or in the **expansion of popcorn kernels** when heated.
 
 
 
• **Chemical leavening:-**
 
 
• It​ involves the use of **baking powder, baking soda, **or other chemical agents to create gas and lift in baked goods.

questions.question: The partially molten upper mantle material called ___________ is a mechanically vulnerable layer beneath the lithosphere characterised by low seismic wave velocity and high attenuation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**asthenosphere.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asthenosphere:-**

 
 
• It is a **partially molten layer **of the **upper mantle **that lies beneath the** lithosphere**, which is the solid, outermost shell of the Earth.
 
• The asthenosphere is characterized by **low seismic wave velocity** and **high attenuation**, which means that seismic waves** slow down** and lose energy as they pass through this layer.
 
• The asthenosphere is** mechanically weak and ductile,** which allows the lithosphere to move and float on top of it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetosphere:-**

 
 
• It is the region around a planet where its **magnetic field is dominant **and protects it from the solar wind.
 
 
 
• **Mesosphere:-**
 
 
• It is the layer of the Earth's atmosphere **above the stratosphere** and **below the thermosphere.**
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere:-**
 
 
• It is the layer of the Earth's atmosphere** above the troposphere **and **below the mesosphere.**
